card.name: Bomba del Chota
card.era: Colonial origins (late 16th-c. African slave labor); consolidated 19th-20th c.
card.tagline: Afro-Ecuadorian drum, song and dance of the Chota Valley.
card.profile: Bomba del Chota is the Afro-Ecuadorian music-and-dance tradition of the Chota-Mira valley on the Imbabura/Carchi border, in communities such as Carpuela, El Juncal, Chalguayacu and La Concepcion (English Wikipedia). The word 'bomba' names the goatskin drum, the genre, and the dance. Couples dance with marked hip movement; women are known for dancing while balancing a bottle on the head (the 'baile de la botella'). Music is built on quatrain coplas with guitar, guiro, requinto and the bomba drum, and a related ensemble, the banda mocha, uses improvised instruments such as dried gourd horns and leaves (Spanish Wikipedia; All Around This World).
card.insight: Distinct from Puerto Rican bomba, the Ecuadorian bomba was certified part of Ecuador's Intangible Cultural Heritage by the INPC and Ministry of Culture on 20 October 2020 as 'La Bomba, musica, danza y saberes ancestrales' - the 18th manifestation certified within a national inventory of 8,327 (INPC).
card.image_significance: Afro-Ecuadorian bottle-balancing dance. A representative image shows colorful regional costume and lively partner or troupe footwork — Chota Valley, Ecuador.
